🗳️ Oakville Votes 2026

Meet the candidates for Mayor of Oakville, explore their ideas, compare local issues, and practise being an informed citizen.

Election Day: October 26, 2026

🏛️ What does a mayor do?

The mayor is the head of Town Council. The mayor helps lead council meetings, represents Oakville, encourages people to take part in local government, and works with councillors on decisions that affect the town.

🚗 Roads & traffic
Local roads and transportation planning
🚌 Transit
Oakville Transit and local transportation
🌳 Parks & recreation
Parks, arenas, pools and community spaces
🏘️ Planning & growth
How land is used and where communities grow
💰 Town budget
How municipal money is raised and spent
❄️ Local services
Services such as snow clearing

Important: The mayor cannot make every decision alone. Town Council votes on many decisions, and some issues also involve Halton Region, Ontario, Canada, or school boards.

🏷️ What political parties are they in?

No political party is listed for any of these mayoral candidates on Oakville’s official certified-candidate list. Ontario municipal candidates may campaign with other like-minded candidates or as a slate, but each person is still an individual candidate with separate campaign finances.

Grade 5 wording: You can say they are running as individual municipal candidates. Avoid saying they all belong to an “Independent Party” — there is no such party listed beside their names on the Oakville ballot.

This is different from many provincial and federal elections, where a candidate’s registered political party may appear with the candidate.

Our inquiry question: If you could vote for Oakville's next mayor, who would you choose — and what evidence supports your decision?

Rob Burton

Big idea: Emphasize experience, continuity, and his record as mayor while responding to Oakville’s growth and development pressures.

CAMPAIGN MESSAGE / PUBLIC RECORD

🏗️ Growth: At the September 29 all-candidates meeting, defended the Town’s approach to Midtown while describing proposed changes to the plan and negotiations with the Province.
💰 Money: His campaign emphasizes his record on taxes and community investment.
🤝 Leadership: Emphasizes experience and working with other levels of government.

💭 Think: When is experience especially helpful for a mayor? When might voters want a different direction?

Arvind Choudhary

Big idea: Change how Town Hall operates, make decisions more open, and make sure infrastructure keeps up with growth.

CAMPAIGN CLAIM

💰 Taxes: Proposes freezing the Town portion of property taxes for 2027 while reviewing spending.
🏗️ Growth: Wants infrastructure and services considered alongside new development.
🗣️ Transparency: Calls for more open decision-making and a lobbyist registry.
🚦 Traffic: Proposes ideas such as smarter traffic signals and improved connections to GO stations.

💭 Think: If a candidate promises to freeze taxes, what questions should a voter ask about services and spending?

Julia Hanna

Big idea: Make sure roads, transit, parks and services are ready as Oakville grows.

CAMPAIGN CLAIM

🏗️ Growth: Says infrastructure should come before major growth.
🚗 Traffic: Proposes a traffic-relief plan focused on roads and intersections.
💰 Money: Proposes an independent budget review and clearer financial reporting.
🗣️ Town Hall: Proposes a lobbyist registry and regular mayor's town halls.

💭 Think: What might “infrastructure before growth” look like in a real neighbourhood?

Jeff Knoll

Big idea: Use long-term planning, clearer financial information and more opportunities for residents to participate.

CAMPAIGN CLAIM

💰 Budget: Emphasizes longer-term financial planning and stronger oversight.
🚌 Transit: Says Oakville should improve transit service and value.
🗣️ Public voice: Proposes stronger public participation and accountability tools.
💼 Business: Wants to attract and grow businesses to broaden Oakville's tax base.

💭 Think: How could having more businesses in town affect residents and municipal finances?

Sean O'Meara

Big idea: Change how Oakville is governed while protecting neighbourhoods and improving transportation and community services.

CAMPAIGN CLAIM

🚗 Transportation: Emphasizes roads, transit and traffic management.
🗣️ Community voice: Wants more resident participation in town decisions.
🌳 Environment: Emphasizes protecting waterfront areas, trees, creeks and green spaces.
💼 Local economy: Supports local businesses and modernizing Town services.

💭 Think: Sometimes protecting neighbourhood character and adding new housing can be in tension. How could a town balance both?
